added_failures_note: The reviewed manifest recorded no baseline_suite or after_suite (both empty). After arm = the reviewed run's own final-gate-guard.log (58 passed, EXIT=0 at a9c815d7). Base arm = measured here with the same command over the two test files that exist at the reviewed base (test_imas_links.py is added by this change), at revision 3fc85aef65d04dbfb98eea2181d2c1c97362a326 whose imas_codex/ingestion and imas_patterns.py are byte-identical to the reviewed base, result 49 passed EXIT=0 (base-arm.log). Pre-existing surface base 49 passed / 0 failed, after 49 passed / 0 failed, so added failures = 0.

findings.text: follow-on: The relationship the section's Done-when names for IDS-name links is REFERENCES_IMAS, but the delivered edge for a bare IDS name is REFERENCES_IDS (graph.py:93, facility.yaml:3436-3442); REFERENCES_IMAS is repurposed to carry DD-path links to IMASNode (graph.py:79-80). Triggering reader: any query or consumer written to the section text that looks for (CodeChunk)-[:REFERENCES_IMAS]->(IDS) now returns zero rows while (CodeChunk)-[:REFERENCES_IDS]->(IDS) holds the 65 JT-60SA links and REFERENCES_IMAS holds the 12 DD-path links. The section's Deliverable text and its Done-when disagree with the base schema (references_imas ranged over IMASNode, not IDS), so the node's split is defensible, but the relationship name is a contract the coordinator should confirm before promoting, because a downstream consumer written to the section words silently sees the wrong edge.

follow-on: The fake graph dispatches on substrings of the Cypher text: query() routes on 'AS mentions' and 'AS linked'; a unit test that reaches the real statements only through recorded-link bookkeeping. If either query string is edited the fake silently returns [] and the assertions become tautological, so the suite cannot catch a mistyped statement - the live EXPLAIN runs (cypher-explain.log, ids-guard-explain.log) are the only thing standing between a query typo and a silent zero, and they are a development receipt, not an automated check.

follow-on: The per-name missing-count query is exercised only against a fake that returns [] for it, so the code path a real graph drives - missing_rows non-empty and missing taken from missing_rows[0]['missing'] - is covered by no test; only the fallback missing = mentions - linked runs in the suite, and only live in ids-guard-live.log. Recorded so a future change to the guard's second query is known to be unpinned.

follow-on: the node's declared write paths included a figures directory (docs/figures/jt60sa-discovery-completion/imas-link-repair) but the fragment carries only a counts table and no figure was written. The section is count-shaped so a table is adequate, and the plan did not require a figure; recorded only so the unused grant is visible.

item_verdicts.call_sites: link_chunks_to_ids_roots is called only at imas_codex/ingestion/pipeline.py:677, inside ingest_files; link_chunks_to_imas_paths keeps its existing call site one line later.
item_verdicts.diff: six files against base 1e6b6e04..78ae9fcb: an IDS-name-to-root linker and a shared count-then-merge helper in graph.py, a Fortran/dot/slash DD-path extractor in extractors/ids.py, two CodeChunk slots and a REFERENCES_IDS edge in facility.yaml, a pipeline call, eight new tests and the fragment, all inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: every JT-60SA chunk with related_ids has a link to each IDS it names (ids_check mentions=65 linked=65 chunks=63), a test with a positive control fails against the old match (negative-control.log, 2 failed EXIT=1), and the link count is in the fragment (65 of 65). The relationship name in the Done-when, REFERENCES_IMAS, is delivered as REFERENCES_IDS - divergence recorded under goal_fidelity.
item_verdicts.goal: the section repairs code ingestion's link from a named IDS to its IDS root and refuses a missing root; imas_codex/ingestion/graph.py:86 adds link_chunks_to_ids_roots and imas_codex/ingestion/pipeline.py:677 calls it in ingest_files.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names eight local commits, records the final focused gate (58 passed EXIT=0 at a9c815d7), the focused-gate logs, cypher-explain.log, the backfill receipt and the negative control, but leaves baseline_suite and after_suite empty, so the added-failure derivation was taken from the reviewer's own base arm against the reviewed run's after arm.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares extractors/ids.py, test_imas_links.py, facility.yaml, graph.py, pipeline.py and the imas-link-repair fragment; the diff touches exactly those six.

justifications.durability: The guard is defended and its refusal is demonstrated, not assumed. test_named_ids_without_a_root_raises asserts the ValueError directly, and test_one_valid_ids_name_does_not_hide_a_missing_name pins the stricter case the section asks for: a valid name in the same batch must not mask a missing one, so graph.py:104-110 checks each name rather than the batch total. negative-control.log proves the pins redden when the old match is restored. All five edited Cypher strings carry a live EXPLAIN, so the real statements are known to parse even though no test executes them. Docked twice. First, the unit tests run against a hand-written fake whose query() dispatches on substrings of the Cypher text ('AS mentions' / 'AS linked'); if either query is edited the fake silently returns [] and the assertions degrade to the fake's own bookkeeping rather than the statement's behaviour, so the suite is coupled to query wording, not query semantics. Second, the per-name missing-count query (graph.py:102-107) is exercised only live in ids-guard-live.log; no test returns a non-empty missing_rows, so the branch that actually raises for a real graph calls uncovered by the suite.
justifications.evidence: Strong and independently reproduced. The old defect reproduces with a positive control: old-link-reproduction.log prints positive_control {'ids_name': 'equilibrium'} [{'roots': 1}] with old_link_result 0, i.e. the root existed and the old query still returned zero - the defect observed, not asserted. The negative control is well-formed: negative-control.log restores the IMASNode id = ids match and makes test_dd_path_links_only_to_existing_imas_node and test_bare_ids_name_links_to_root fail by name with EXIT=1, so the new pins redden on the regression they guard, and the raised text 'No IDS roots linked for 1 named references' is the guard itself firing. All five edited Cypher statements carry live EXPLAIN (cypher-explain.log four, ids-guard-explain.log one). The backfill receipt is a stored-chunk-only run (jt60sa-backfill.log: extraction scanned 3307, updated 71, path_candidates 26; function_results ids_linked 65, paths_linked 12) with no facility-host request. I re-ran an independent base arm myself: 49 passed EXIT=0 over test_code_ingest_idempotent.py and test_graph/test_schema_context.py at a revision (3fc85aef65d04dbfb98eea2181d2c1c97362a326) whose imas_codex/ingestion and imas_patterns.py are byte-identical to the reviewed base (git diff empty), giving added failures 0 against the reviewed run's own after arm (final-gate-guard.log 58 passed EXIT=0). Docked for one provenance issue: two gate-log headers name a revision that does not describe their content. extractor-test.log records revision=1e6b6e04 and runs tests/ingestion/test_imas_links.py, but that file is absent from 1e6b6e04 (git cat-file -e fails; the diff shows it added at c03fbefc8), so the file was untracked when the log was written. focused-gate-retry.log records revision=2b70aaa5 as passing while focused-gate.log at the same revision recorded 4 failures, and the fix that removed them was not committed until 12cbe0745 at 05:11, one minute after the retry log's timestamp - the green retry ran against uncommitted content. Neither is a false measurement, but a reader reconciling header revision to tree is misled in both.
justifications.fit: Follows the module's idioms closely. The two linkers share one helper, _link_chunk_references (graph.py:118), instead of duplicating the count-then-merge Cypher, and the four comment rewrites in link_chunks_to_data_nodes move step-numbers to mechanism descriptions, which is the repository's stated preference. The extractor reuses extract_imas_paths / normalize_imas_path / get_known_ids rather than re-implementing path parsing. Comments describe mechanism and the added symbols carry no plan label. Docked twice, both minor. The helper interpolates property_name, target_label and relationship into Cypher with an f-string; both call sites pass module-private constants, so it is not injectable, but it is the interpolation shape the graph guidance asks callers to keep constant. The docstring on link_chunks_to_imas_paths was narrowed to 'Link extracted DD paths to existing IMASNode paths only', while its module docstring still lists IMASNode among 'data entities' without the bare-name-to-IDS-root path now handled by its sibling.
justifications.goal_fidelity: VERDICT: goal met with a documented naming divergence. The delivered code links every named IDS to its IDS root and refuses a missing one, so the substance of the section holds: link_chunks_to_ids_roots at imas_codex/ingestion/graph.py:86 returns 65 of 65 JT-60SA IDS mentions linked across 63 chunks (jt60sa-backfill.log ids_check mentions=65 linked=65 chunks=63; ids-guard-live.log remaining [{'missing': 0}]), and it raises ValueError on any unresolved name. The divergence: the doc's Done-when names a REFERENCES_IMAS relationship to each IDS a chunk names, but the delivered edge for bare IDS names is REFERENCES_IDS (facility.yaml:3436-3442), while REFERENCES_IMAS is repurposed to carry DD-path links to IMASNode (graph.py:79-80). Any downstream reader or query written to the section text looks for REFERENCES_IMAS to an IDS root and now finds DD-path links to IMASNode instead. The section's own wording is internally inconsistent - its Deliverable says 'the IDS root nodes the schema declares as the REFERENCES_IMAS target', yet at the reviewed base references_imas ranged over IMASNode, not IDS, so no such IDS target existed. The node resolved that by adding a second, correctly-typed edge rather than repointing references_imas to IDS; that is defensible and better typed, but it is a relationship-name decision the section does not settle and the coordinator should confirm against its consumers.
justifications.reuse: Good reuse. The reference extraction is a thin wrapper over the existing imas_codex/discovery/base/imas_patterns helpers (extract_imas_paths, normalize_imas_path, get_known_ids) rather than a parallel parser, and the Fortran-chain handling is added beside them. The  two linkers converge on the single _link_chunk_references helper, so the count-then-merge shape and its empty-result tolerance are written once. pipeline._split_and_extract feeds both extractions from one pass over chunk.text. No second implementation of IDS-name extraction or path normalization was introduced.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-status 1e6b6e04..78ae9fcb1 is exactly six files and exactly the declared write paths, nothing else: docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/imas-link-repair.html (A), imas_codex/ingestion/extractors/ids.py (M), imas_codex/ingestion/graph.py (M), imas_codex/ingestion/pipeline.py (M), imas_codex/schemas/facility.yaml (M), tests/ingestion/test_imas_links.py (A). imas_codex/schemas/facility.yaml was added to the grant after the first attempt's NEEDS-HELP and the node used it only for the two CodeChunk slots and the references_ids edge. The worktree is clean at 78ae9fcb. All eight commits are conventional with a subject AND a body. A case-insensitive scan of all eight messages for co-authored-by / generated with / claude / copilot returns zero hits. A plan/phase/ticket label scan over the changed paths is clean; the new file and symbols are named by mechanism (extract_imas_path_references, link_chunks_to_ids_roots). No branch created, nothing pushed.
